note: Shape screening of the protected core. Closes the identifier-rename blind spot that docs/ip/dependency-similarity-screening.json measured on itself and published.

closes.blindSpot: A verbatim 1838-line copy with every non-keyword identifier renamed is detected by none of the token screening's three methods, because normalisation replaces strings, numbers, comments and whitespace but not identifiers.
closes.howClosed: Shape is compared instead of text: each file is reduced to the pre-order sequence of its syntax node kinds, so a renamed copy is identical.

parsers.crossLanguage: Python node ids are offset past the whole TypeScript SyntaxKind enum, so a cross-language match cannot occur even by accident.

calibration.principle: A reporting threshold is worth nothing unless the scores it cleared are published beside it.
calibration.conclusion: Nothing lies between 0.067 and 0.93. The threshold could be moved anywhere in that range without changing a single result.

knownBlindSpots: Fragments. Similarity is Jaccard over the whole file, so a small piece lifted from a large one scores low. Measured: the renamed pydantic/main.py cut to 853 of its 6879 nodes scores 0.096. Both screenings detect whole-file derivatives; neither detects a copied function inside an otherwise original file.
128 protected files have fewer than 200 shape nodes and are not compared, because a shape that small is shared by every codebase.
.sql and .css have no parser here and remain the unscreened 28 named in the token record.
A shape match is evidence of structure, not proof of copying: two independent implementations of the same small pattern can share a shape. Nothing reached that point in this run.
establishes: No file among the 532 compared is a copy of a dependency of this repository, including a copy whose identifiers were renamed, and none is a partial derivative of one above 0.75 shape similarity.
doesNotEstablish: Anything about fragments, about the 128 files below the floor, about the 28 files with no parser, about a corpus outside our own dependencies, or about authorship, which is a separate claim with separate evidence.

wholeRepository.why: The core is where the crown jewels are, but it is not where borrowed code is likeliest to land: nobody reviews the application shell. Screening only the boundary and reporting the result as originality is the same coverage overstatement this programme already made once, with Python.

finding.matches: msw@2.13.2 mockServiceWorker.js across four package resolutions
finding.note: The same file the repository-wide token screening independently identified. Two methods sharing no code, one answer, and it is the only third-party file either finds.

calibration.explanation: Every file above 0.2 is a message dictionary, a lexicon or a barrel of re-exports. A dictionary and happy-dom's CSS property table are both one large nested object literal, so they share a shape for a reason that has nothing to do with either of them. This is the convergence the methodology predicts, seen rather than assumed.
calibration.conclusion: The threshold is worth more here than in the core run: the empty band it sits in is 0.39 to 0.93, measured against real structural coincidence rather than against nothing.
